hook_text: Every rand that moves through a hair salon ends up in one of two books. Here is how accountants decide which.
clip_script: Monday, braids, card tap: six hundred rand in. Tuesday, three cash haircuts: more in. Wednesday, rent by app: six thousand out. Friday, wages by EFT: out. Each one is a transaction, something that changes the business's money and can be counted in rand. And in accounting, cash means paid now: card, EFT or notes. Paid later is credit. Now picture two boxes on the counter. Money-in documents, receipts, till rolls, transfer proofs, go into the cash receipts journal. Money-out documents, EFT confirmations, supplier slips, debit orders, go into the cash payments journal. No document, no entry. At month-end each column gets one total. That is how a salon's chaos becomes clean books.
visual_style: A whiteboard salon counter with two labelled boxes, slips flying into each, then each box opening into a journal page with columns adding up to a total.
mood: Organised and satisfying, chaos turning into order.
pacing: Fast day-by-day montage, a pause on the two boxes, a neat totalling finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort every transaction into the right book.
